question: Can gravity be a universally stronger maximum field whose source vectors are only partly completed in the Solar System, with the completion fraction changing universally with tidal curvature and vector coherence?

root_equation.field: partial_i[K_ij(Sigma) partial_j Phi] - Q(Sigma)/c^2 partial_t^2 Phi = 4 pi G_solar rho_b
root_equation.flux_relation: D_g=K g; div(D_g)=-4 pi G_solar rho_b
root_equation.solar_limit: T >> T_star implies C=C_solar and g=g_bar exactly
root_equation.maximum_limit: T << T_star and full vector availability imply C=1 and g/g_bar=1/C_solar

sample.bridge: 44 MaNGA BCG points plus 72 density-resolved CLASH radial points
sample.bridge_objective: equal-domain mean of equal-system mean squared log residual
sample.SPARC: 131 galaxies; nuisance parameters fit on 2066 inner points and tested on 968 untouched outer points
sample.raw_lensing: RX J2129 15 training and 7 already-spent heldout image positions
sample.cluster_target_warning: CLASH acceleration target is deprojected from fitted NFW lensing profiles

coherence_completion.coherence_warning: BCG Lambda_Re, cluster zero-coherence, and SPARC one-minus-bulge-force fraction are only provisional cross-domain proxies.

selection.rule: lowest five-fold heldout bridge equal-domain RMSE; raw images and SPARC are not used for selection

claim_limits: This is a weak-field constitutive law, not yet a covariant action.
A bounded completion law is observationally equivalent to an environment-dependent enhancement relative to locally measured G; the interpretation alone is not new evidence.
The scalar tidal proxy g_bar/r is not the full three-dimensional tidal tensor.
The coherence observables are not geometrically identical across BCG, cluster, and SPARC samples.
RX J2129 coordinates are an already-inspected diagnostic, not an independent holdout.
